 Poland v Sweden Prediction: 7/4 Isak can punish hosts
 Partner Authors
 Updated: 8 hours ago
 Poland are out of the running for a top two finish and their final mission is to try to defend third place as they get ready to take on sectional winners Sweden at Wrocław Stadium on Tuesday. 
 It has been a tough year for the Poles, who missed out on a place at the 2026 World Cup before struggling in the Nations League's second tier.
 Jan Urban's side were the top seeds in Group B4, but have accumulated just four points and were beaten for the third time on Saturday when losing 2-1 at fourth-placed Romania.
 All that is left is to try to stay above the Romanians and secure a third-place finish which would guarantee the retention of League B status.
 But they must be anticipating a tough test against Sweden, who have beaten them twice this year - securing a 3-2 triumph in the World Cup qualifying play-offs and a 3-1 Nations League victory.
 Sweden had a mixed time at the World Cup where they bowed out with a 3-0 loss to France at the round of 32.
 But they have developed a winning habit in the Nations League and are assured of top spot with a game to spare after Saturday’s 3-2 success at home to Bosnia-Herzegovina.

 Poland v Sweden Prediction
 Best Bet: Sweden to win @ 2/1 
 Sweden have secured promotion to Nations League A and they can round off a superb campaign with their fifth victory in six games.
 There could be some interesting selection calls from Sweden head coach Graham Potter, who has the option of freshening up his side.
 But Potter will be keen to keep standards high as he focuses on getting players ready for the challenge of Euro 2028 qualification.
 While 2026 have been a year of progress for Sweden, it has been a time to forget for Poland, who seem to be approaching a tricky transitional phase.
 Robert Lewandowski rolled back the years with a hat-trick in their 6-0 victory at home to Romania, but the other five matches have been a major disappointment.
 Poland failed to score against Bosnia (drawing 0-0 at home and losing 1-0 away), but their biggest disappointment came in Bucharest at the weekend where they lost 2-1 to Romania.
 They look like a side short of quality and confidence and may struggle to stop the Swedes from defeating them for a third time in eight months.
 Alternative Bet: Alexander Isak anytime goalscorer @ 7/4 
 Victor Gyokeres has led the Swedish surge, scoring six of their ten Nations League goals, but his strike partner Alexander Isak could be the match-winner against the Poles.
 Isak is having a strong season for Liverpool , scoring seven goals in nine Premier League appearances, and could be the man to expose a suspect Poland defence weakened by the absence of suspended Porto defender Jakub Kiwior.

 Sweden have beaten Poland twice this year, scoring six goals in the process, and the contest in Wroclaw should be another entertaining affair.
 The obvious threat from Poland comes from Robert Lewandowski, who will be looking to add to his 92-goal international tally.
 But Poland showed defensive vulnerability in their weekend loss to Romania and they face a tougher examination from Sweden, who have netted ten goals across the five games.
 Sweden’s preferred 4-4-2 formation allows them to get Isak and Gyokeres in the same side.
 But it also places a heavy defensive responsibility on the central midfielders, including Brighton’s Yasin Ayari, who looks overpriced for a booking.
 Ayari has escaped punishment despite committing five fouls across the campaign, but his luck may be about to run out.
